dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation

evidence.note: Inspected all graph files and the reference alignment: extracted exact node/edge counts for both pairs and the tab-separated alignment format, confirming faithful format parsing.
Built a scorer reproducing S3/NC and computed the reference alignment's actual S3=0.248 — accurate reproduction of the metric definitions plus instance calibration.

Repeated quantitative reasoning about the S3 denominator: max Ea=E1 bounds, min achievable E2 from lowest-degree subsets, and the Ea/E2 targets required to reach 0.55 — instance-specific analysis of what S3 is achievable.

Applied and named multiple established methods (SANA-style annealing on S3, Hungarian assignment, spectral embeddings, seed-and-extend), and exploited the provided reference alignment as a warm start / NC anchor — instance leverage.

Coding began early (step 12) and method analysis was interleaved with implementation; no external literature survey was ever conducted despite the task encouraging it — the ceiling separating this from a 10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent decisively clears anchor 5 (correct format parsing, faithful S3/NC reproduction, recognizing the known problem class) and reaches anchor 8 through strong instance probing — quantifying network sizes/density, computing achievable S3 bounds from the E2/Ea structure, and exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start — while applying and naming several established methods (SANA-style SA, Hungarian, spectral, seed-and-extend). It falls short of 10 because it never performed the encouraged literature survey (relying on prior knowledge, naming SANA only in passing) and its analysis was interleaved with early coding rather than synthesized up front.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables

evidence.note: Cleanly separated pipeline stages up front: built score.py (parser+scorer) as shared infrastructure, then a greedy baseline aligner, then optimizers — a real parse→score→align→optimize decomposition.

Both thresholds treated as explicit milestones and broken into derived numeric sub-targets (e.g. required Ea/E2 to reach S3=0.55); recognized DM-HS (S3 only) as easier than yeast (S3+NC), showing awareness of the two-deliverable asymmetry.

Instead of a single generic reusable aligner, wrote ~20 near-duplicate one-off scripts (opt3, targeted_opt, aggressor, robust_opt, grid_search, final_sa, etc.), i.e. failed to factor shared aligner infrastructure from per-instance tuning — the duplicated effort the task structure warned against.

Despite repeatedly noting DM-HS was the easier bar, it deferred that deliverable to the very end and produced only a broken S3=0.010 result; the two-deliverable sequencing was recognized but not executed deliberately.
Final submission with y2kr-SC S3=0.396 and DM-HS S3=0.010 confirms decomposition never resolved into a working per-deliverable milestone completion despite the stated stage structure.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly cleared anchor 5: distinct parse/score/align/optimize/write stages with both numeric thresholds treated as explicit per-deliverable milestones, plus repeated derivation of numeric sub-targets. But it stops short of anchor 8: it never factored a generic reusable aligner (instead rewriting ~20 duplicate scripts, only the scorer was shared) and it recognized but mismanaged the DM-HS-vs-yeast sequencing, neglecting the easier deliverable until it failed. That places the observed behavior between 5 and 8, at a 6.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking

evidence.note: Builds /app/score.py early to compute S3 and NC, then runs it on the reference alignment (expecting NC=1.0 vs itself, finding S3=0.248) — an implicit correctness sanity check on both metrics.
Scorer's components (Ea=11063, E2_aligned=39556, S3=0.248) are arithmetically consistent with the spec's S3 = Ea/(E1+E2_aligned-Ea), showing the E2_aligned denominator term is implemented faithfully.
Correctly computes NC against the provided reference to the exact node count (713 vs needed 714 for 0.30 threshold), demonstrating NC matches spec and reference.

Uses score.py repeatedly to measure both deliverables before submitting and reports true scores (yeast 0.396, DM-HS 0.010) rather than assuming success; scorer also surfaced an invalid Ea=0/E2=0 mapping (step 145), catching a format bug.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent implemented a faithful S3/NC scorer matching the spec (including the E2_aligned denominator) and used it continuously to measure every deliverable before finishing, honestly reporting sub-threshold scores — clearing the level-5 bar. It partially reaches toward level 8 via a reference-vs-itself NC=1.0 sanity check, precise NC-vs-reference counting, and catching a malformed output through scoring. But it never cross-checked the scorer on a tiny hand-computable case, nor enforced injectivity/coverage/exact-name validity as explicit assertions, so it falls short of full level-8 airtightness. That places it at a 6.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs

evidence.note: Established and repeatedly re-used baselines/targets: greedy S3=0.031, reference S3=0.248 (Ea=11063, E2=39556), and per-deliverable bars (yeast>=0.55/NC>=0.30, DM-HS>=0.32). Consistently framed the gap to target.

Read intermediate SA progress reports and logged the objective over iterations (iter100 S3=0.347, iter150 S3=0.363, iter60000 S3=0.376, iter90000 S3=0.38), reasoning live about required Ea vs current E2 to judge whether the trajectory could still reach target.

Detected plateau/thrashing explicitly: 'swap-only SA didn't improve (stuck at 0.382)', 'SA moving to worse solutions but not finding better ones (best 0.396, current 0.179)', and used this to kill converged runs and restart with new parameters.

Maintained an accurate running best-so-far per deliverable throughout ('yeast best S3=0.394 (need 0.55), DM-HS best S3=0.005 (need 0.32)') and verified final scores with an independent scorer before submitting.

DM-HS was monitored almost only at endpoints (0.005 / 0.010) rather than tracked over iterations; despite repeatedly noting DM-HS was the 'easier' target, it never successfully reallocated compute there, leaving it far below bar — falls short of the level-10 marginal-gain allocation.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly logged the objective over iterations, distinguished continued gains from plateau/thrashing, and used that read to decide when to stop, kill, and restart runs — matching the level-8 anchor. It always knew the per-deliverable best-so-far and gap to target. It falls short of 10 because the ledger was informal and scattered (amid repeated terminal-state confusion), the DM-HS deliverable received only endpoint scoring rather than iteration-level monitoring, and it failed to reallocate remaining compute toward the deliverable where marginal gain was highest despite recognizing DM-HS was easier.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed

evidence.note: After greedy degree matching yields S3=0.031 and the reference itself only 0.248, the agent diagnoses the root cause (E2_aligned=39556 too dense; max S3~0.406 even with perfect Ea) and pivots strategy: spectral embedding, low-degree starts, then targeted high-degree-node replacement to reduce E2. Genuine WHY-diagnosis driving new levers, not blind reruns.

Exploits the reference alignment for the NC bar: keeps a fraction (KEEP_FRAC) of reference mappings to hold NC>=0.30, and corrects 0.30->0.31 when NC came out to 0.2997. This is exactly the anchor-8 'exploit the reference for the yeast NC' move, with re-measurement confirming NC=0.50.

Repeatedly reasons quantitatively about why S3 plateaus (computes required Ea given current E2, notes swaps can't change E2 so replacement moves are needed, detects SA 'stuck at 0.396 = initialization'). Strong plateau diagnosis feeding targeted algorithm changes (swap vs replace moves, degree-penalty tuning).

Mid/late trajectory shows heavy repetition of the SAME core family (keep X% reference + Hungarian degree-penalty replace + SA) across keep_frac 0.30/0.31/0.50/0.70 and grid search, all plateauing ~0.37-0.40. These are meaningful but converged re-runs — dragging behavior toward the lower anchors.

Weak best-solution preservation: DM-HS is overwritten repeatedly and ends at S3=0.010 (a regression vs. intermediate attempts), and final yeast 0.396 is essentially the initialization value, not a preserved best. Much late effort is process-kill chaos rather than crisp keep/revert cycles — falls short of anchor-10 discipline.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent clearly clears anchor 5 (changes meaningful levers and re-measures) and demonstrates anchor-8 behavior throughout: it diagnoses WHY targets are missed (dense E2 caps S3, swaps can't reduce E2, NC needs reference retention), makes targeted interventions (Hungarian degree penalties, swap-vs-replace moves, reference-keeping for NC), and confirms via re-scoring. However it falls short of anchor 10 because it does not decisively preserve best-known solutions (final DM-HS regressed to 0.010), repeatedly re-runs the same keep-reference+Hungarian+SA family at a plateau, and late work devolves into process-management thrashing rather than clean hypothesis->intervention->keep/revert cycles. That places it at 7 — strong, well-diagnosed course-correction with imperfect improvement-cycle discipline.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation

evidence.note: Runs consistently bounded with timeout (120/180/300/600s), showing awareness of wall-clock cost rather than unbounded execution.
Monitored intermediate convergence (iter 100 S3=0.347, iter 150 S3=0.363) and reasoned it would 'cap around 0.36-0.40' — run-length decisions informed by observed score-improvement rate.
Launched the same oversized full Hungarian (~105M entries) that hung and had to be killed, then repeated the identical mistake later — wasted compute, failing to learn from observed cost.
Grid search deliberately used 'short SA (50000 iterations each)' to fit multiple configs into the budget — time-aware sizing of per-run length.
DM-HS was starved of compute and ended at S3=0.010 while yeast consumed most of the budget — poor split between the two deliverables, though a best yeast solution (0.396) was banked to disk.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent bounded every run with escalating timeouts, monitored convergence to judge whether iteration counts would reach targets, shortened per-config SA to fit budget, and ensured both files were produced with a banked yeast solution — squarely matching anchor 5. It does not reach anchor 8: the budget split was actively poor (yeast hoarded compute while easier-looking DM-HS was neglected to S3=0.010), and it repeatedly wasted time relaunching an oversized Hungarian that predictably hung, showing no systematic probe-then-right-size calibration.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon, open-ended research/optimization task: align two pairs of PPI networks to hit specific S3 (and NC) thresholds. Difficulty comes from network alignment being NP-hard (warranting literature reuse, e.g. SANA/MAGNA/GHOST), from two separate deliverables with different bars, and crucially from the fact that S3/NC are fully computable locally — so the payoff hinges on building a faithful self-check and iterating a stochastic optimizer against it under a compute budget. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, verification, and adaptive iteration; decomposition is moderate.

dimensions.name: Problem & literature orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the graph format, the exact S3/NC definitions, and surveying known network-alignment methods before committing to an approach.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Network alignment is NP-hard; naive greedy approaches rarely clear S3>=0.55. Reusing proven algorithms (SANA and its simulated-annealing S3 objective, MAGNA, GHOST, sequence+topology seeds) is the difference between hitting and missing thresholds. Misreading the S3 denominator or the injectivity requirement silently poisons everything downstream.

anchors.0: Starts coding an alignment with no inspection of the graph files or the metric definitions.
anchors.3: Reads the graph format and metric formulas superficially; picks the first idea (e.g. degree-sorted greedy) with no awareness of the field.
anchors.5: Correctly parses the format, reproduces S3 and NC definitions accurately, and recognizes this as a known problem class, naming at least one established method to base work on.
anchors.8: Deliberately researches specific network-alignment methods (e.g. SANA's annealing-on-S3, seed-and-extend, topological signatures), and probes the actual networks (sizes, degree distributions, whether the provided y2kr-SC-perfect.align can seed or bound the search) to choose an approach fit to THIS data.
anchors.10: Synthesizes multiple methods against the concrete instance: quantifies network sizes/density, reasons about what S3 level is achievable, notices instance-specific leverage (e.g. Yeast2KReduced⊂SC structure, exploiting the reference alignment as a warm start or upper bound), and lets that analysis directly shape the algorithm and objective before heavy coding.

dimensions.name: Pipeline decomposition across two deliverables
dimensions.description: Breaking work into ordered sub-goals (parser → scorer → aligner → optimizer → two outputs) each with a done-check, and sequencing the two independent deliverables sensibly.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are two distinct targets with different thresholds and a shared toolchain. Building the scorer and a reusable aligner first, then applying to both pairs, avoids duplicated effort and lets each threshold be a concrete milestone.

anchors.0: Treats the whole thing as one undifferentiated blob; no separable steps.
anchors.3: Vague ordering in prose; no explicit done-criteria per step.
anchors.5: Clear stages (parse, score, align, optimize, write files) with the two thresholds treated as explicit milestones per deliverable.
anchors.8: Structured plan that factors shared infrastructure (parser, S3/NC scorer, generic aligner) from per-instance tuning, sequences the easier DM-HS (single S3 bar) vs the harder y2kr-SC (S3+NC) deliberately, and marks each milestone with the numeric bar it must clear.
anchors.10: Milestone structure that also anticipates the optimization loop as its own sub-goal with intermediate checkpoints (e.g. 'reach S3=0.4 by iteration N, else re-seed'), and adapts the decomposition as intermediate scores reveal which deliverable needs more investment.

dimensions.name: Faithful local metric self-checking
dimensions.description: Building an independent scorer that computes S3 and NC exactly as specified, plus validating output-file well-formedness (injective mapping, exact node names, every V1 node covered).
dimensions.why_it_matters: The grader's metric is fully reproducible offline. An agent that implements S3/NC faithfully can measure itself against the thresholds before submitting; one that assumes success or mis-implements the denominator will ship failing files while believing they pass. This is the single highest-leverage meta-move on this task.

anchors.0: No local scoring; submits alignments without measuring S3/NC.
anchors.3: Some ad hoc sanity check (e.g. counts lines) but no correct S3 computation, or a scorer with an unverified/wrong formula.
anchors.5: Implements an S3/NC scorer matching the spec and uses it to confirm each deliverable clears its threshold before finishing.
anchors.8: Scorer is validated for correctness (e.g. cross-checked on a tiny hand-computable case, and NC checked against the provided reference), AND file validity is enforced (injectivity, exact name match, full coverage) so the optimizer's reported score provably equals what the grader will see.
anchors.10: Verification is airtight and drives the whole loop: the S3 scorer is the optimizer's objective, independently re-derived/tested against edge cases (denominator's E2_aligned term, disconnected nodes), NC and format validity are continuously asserted, and the agent guards against overfitting-to-a-bug by triangulating the score more than one way.

dimensions.name: Tracking score progress over optimization runs
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of current S3/NC vs targets across (potentially long) stochastic optimization, detecting plateaus/thrashing and knowing which deliverable still falls short.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Simulated-annealing / iterative aligners run for many iterations with noisy improvement. Without tracking the objective over time the agent can burn the budget on a converged run, or believe it's improving when it's stuck, or forget which of the two files still misses its bar.

anchors.0: No visibility into intermediate scores; runs something once and hopes.
anchors.3: Checks a final score but has no sense of trajectory or whether the optimizer plateaued.
anchors.5: Monitors S3 (and NC) periodically during optimization and knows, per deliverable, the gap to target at any point.
anchors.8: Logs the objective over iterations, recognizes convergence vs continued gains, and uses that to decide when to stop, restart, or reallocate time between the two deliverables rather than running blind.
anchors.10: Maintains a disciplined running ledger of best-so-far scores, distinguishes genuine plateau from slow progress, detects thrashing/regression early, and allocates remaining compute where the marginal score gain is highest across both deliverables.

dimensions.name: Course-correction when a target is missed
dimensions.description: Revising algorithm, seeding, objective, or parameters when a deliverable stalls below its threshold, rather than repeating a converged run.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A first approach (e.g. greedy topological match) may plateau below S3=0.55 or NC=0.30. Progress requires switching strategy — better seeds, annealing, sequence signals, exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast pair — instead of re-running the same thing.

anchors.0: Barrels ahead on the initial approach even when it clearly falls short; never changes tack.
anchors.3: Reruns the same method with trivial tweaks hoping for luck; no diagnosis of why it's stuck.
anchors.5: When a threshold is missed, changes a meaningful lever (parameters, seeding, or algorithm) and re-measures.
anchors.8: Diagnoses WHY a target is missed (e.g. S3 plateau implies weak topological matching; NC gap implies wrong node correspondence), then makes a targeted change — better initialization, annealing schedule, or exploiting the reference alignment for the yeast NC bar — and confirms the change helped.
anchors.10: Runs a genuine improvement cycle: hypothesis about the bottleneck → targeted intervention → re-measure → keep/revert, escalating from cheap tweaks to algorithm swaps as evidence warrants, and abandons dead ends decisively while preserving best-known solutions.

dimensions.name: Optimizer compute-budget allocation
dimensions.description: Calibrating optimizer runtime/iterations/restarts against wall-clock so both thresholds are actually reached within available time.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Stochastic network aligners can run arbitrarily long; a HSapiens-scale search is expensive. Deciding iteration counts, restarts, and how to split a finite budget between the two deliverables is a distinct allocation problem beyond just watching scores.

anchors.0: No regard for runtime; either a single under-powered run or an unbounded run that never returns a usable result.
anchors.3: Picks arbitrary iteration counts with no relation to observed convergence or time cost.
anchors.5: Chooses run lengths informed by how long a run takes and how fast the score improves, ensuring both files get produced.
anchors.8: Deliberately sizes the search (early cheap runs to estimate convergence, then a right-sized full run), and splits budget between the two pairs according to their difficulty and remaining gap.
anchors.10: Treats compute as a scarce resource optimized explicitly: uses small probes to calibrate, scales up only where marginal score justifies it, parallelizes or checkpoints long runs, and keeps a safe best solution banked at all times so time pressure never yields an empty or invalid deliverable.
